source_items.content_summary: Horizontal projectile motion has zero horizontal acceleration in the ideal model.
Vertical projectile motion has constant downward acceleration g.

required_concepts.title: Resolve launch velocity into x and y components
Use the same time in both component descriptions

forbidden_inventions: Do not add air resistance or horizontal acceleration to this ideal-model bucket.

questions.prompt_summary: Resolve the projectile velocity into horizontal and vertical components at a stated instant.
assumptions: Use the model conditions stated in Revised Core (2) v2 and the linked Core (1A) bucket.

assumptions: Use the model conditions stated in Revised Core (2) v2 and the linked Core (1A) bucket.

Keep the same horizontal component while the vertical component changes.

learning_atoms.title: Resolve one launch vector
learning_atoms.purpose: Show that one velocity arrow can be described by horizontal and vertical components.
visual_stages: Stage 1: draw the launch arrow u at angle theta
teaching_moves: draw the launch arrow u at angle theta
misconception_targets: u_x and u_y are each equal to the full launch speed
checks: Resolve a fresh launch arrow without help.

learning_atoms.title: Horizontal motion keeps its component
visual_stages: Stage 1: show equal horizontal spacing at equal times
teaching_moves: show equal horizontal spacing at equal times
misconception_targets: gravity also accelerates the projectile horizontally
checks: Explain why v_x stays constant in the ideal model.

learning_atoms.title: Vertical motion changes under gravity
learning_atoms.purpose: Build the signed vertical component model.
visual_stages: Stage 3: show v_y shrinking to zero
Stage 4: show v_y negative during descent
checks: State the sign of v_y while descending.

learning_atoms.title: One projectile uses one clock
learning_atoms.purpose: Synchronise x and y descriptions at the same instant.
visual_stages: Stage 1: show t=0 in both component views
Stage 2: show t=1 in both views
Stage 3: show t=2 in both views
Stage 4: recombine x(t),y(t) into one point
teaching_moves: show t=0 in both component views
misconception_targets: x and y can be evaluated at unrelated times and still describe one position
checks: Explain why x(2 s) and y(3 s) cannot be one projectile position.

transfer_families.title: Velocity components at a stated instant
recognition_signals: a launch speed and angle are given
a horizontal or vertical component is required
a later instant may be stated

method_steps.title: Resolve once
method_steps.learner_move: Write u_x=u cos(theta) and u_y=u sin(theta).

method_steps.title: Use the shared clock
method_steps.learner_move: Use the same t in the x and y component equations.

method_steps.title: Check the event
method_steps.learner_move: Confirm signs, units and whether an apex prerequisite is required.

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile is launched at 20 m/s at 30 degrees. Find its horizontal and vertical velocity components after 1 s for g=10 m/s^2.
independent_practice.answer_check: u_x=10*sqrt(3) m/s and v_y=0 m/s at t=1 s.

hint_ladder.label: Representation
hint_ladder.prompt: Draw u_x horizontally and u_y vertically.

hint_ladder.label: First move
hint_ladder.prompt: Start with u_x=u cos(theta), u_y=u sin(theta).

readiness_checks: FIRST_MOVE: write the component equations without a hint.
FINISH: solve a fresh case and check signs.
